solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Team's backed favourite dodge

indicators.note: something backed is moved in reverse, so the word for favourite is read from its end

blocks.note: a side is a team; with the 's it reads side's
a teacher's pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A sports team's star player has slipped away from some trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: SIDE'S plus PET reversed (TEP) gives SIDESTEP.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep a question or tackle is to evade it, a verb synonym of dodge.

clue.text: Disparage the writer's excellent example

blocks.note: the writer is the setter, I; the writer's = I'm, I am
a peach is a lovely, excellent specimen of something

explanation.surface: Someone is belittling a piece of writing others hold up as a model.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'the writer' is the setter, so 'the writer's' becomes I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach someone's honesty is to call it into question and so discredit it, a formal sense close to disparage.

clue.text: Eastern European country coming up strange

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the letters run from bottom to top, back to front

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for east or eastern
Eire is the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.surface: An Eastern European state is starting to seem odd.
explanation.walkthrough: E then EIRE written upwards (ERIE) gives EERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means uncanny or weird in an unsettling way, a synonym of strange.

clue.text: Youngster's cropped top

indicators.note: cropped means cut short, so the final letter of the word is snipped off

blocks.note: a teen is a teenager, a youngster

explanation.surface: A teenager is wearing a crop top.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as 'is': the youngster is cropped. 'Cropped top' looks like one garment, but cropped belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A tee is a T-shirt, an item of clothing worn on the upper body, which is a top.

clue.text: Painful day engaged in arrangement of hair for elephant?

definitions.note: the question mark flags the elephant as one example of the answer

indicators.note: things engaged in something are held within it, so these letters go inside the hairstyle word

blocks.note: achy means hurting, painful
D is the abbreviation for day
a perm is a permanent wave, a hair arrangement

explanation.surface: A painful day at the hairdresser's, apparently for an elephant.
explanation.walkthrough: The hairdressing surface hides that 'arrangement of hair' is a single word that wraps around the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A pachyderm is a thick-skinned mammal, and the elephant is the best-known example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Unhappy, having to import new grains

indicators.note: to import is to bring something inside, so the letter for new is taken into the word for unhappy

blocks.note: sad means unhappy
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A trader is gloomy about being forced to bring in a fresh supply of grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grains' suggests cereal, but it means tiny particles of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Sand is a mass of tiny loose grains of rock, so grains collectively serve as a plural definition.

clue.text: Has unusual amount to pay up for vegetable

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so the letters of has fall out of their normal order
in a down entry, up means the letters are written bottom to top, back to front

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a toll is a fee one must pay, for a road or bridge

explanation.surface: Someone owes an odd sum and must settle up for some vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: SHA from the rearranged has, then TOLL upwards (LLOT), gives SHALLOT. 'Pay up' looks like settling a bill, but up belongs to the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallot is a small mild bulb of the onion family, a kitchen vegetable.

clue.text: Dark period close to end of plot

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter only of the word that follows

blocks.note: nigh means near, close
the last letter of plot

explanation.surface: A grim stretch of a story as the plot nears its conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: Close here is the adjective meaning near, not the verb or noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the time between sunset and sunrise when it is dark.

clue.text: Encourage reduction in gush?

indicators.note: a reduction makes the word shorter, so its last letter is dropped

blocks.note: a spurt is a sudden gush of liquid

explanation.surface: Could cutting the flow of water be a way to encourage someone?
explanation.definitionFit: To spur someone on is to urge or goad them, as a rider's spur urges a horse.

clue.text: Coppers pursuing former partner in money business

blocks.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
coppers are low-value coins, small change

explanation.surface: Police officers are chasing someone's ex-partner over a financial matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pursuing' only fixes the order: the coins come after the former partner. Coppers looks like police, but it means copper coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Exchange is the business of converting one currency into another, as at a bureau de change.

clue.text: Canal, say — unpleasantly raw and wet indeed

indicators.note: unpleasantly suggests things turned nasty and out of shape, so the following letters get rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of raw and wet together, to be rearranged
ay (aye) is yes, indeed

explanation.surface: A canal is described as cold, raw and very wet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' is part of the anagram phrase, joining the two words to be mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal is one kind of navigable channel, an example of the answer as 'say' signals.

clue.text: Swigs ale freely, clutching new drink container

indicators.note: freely means without restraint, so the letters move about at will
to clutch is to hold tight, so the rearranged letters wrap around the letter for new

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A drinker glugs beer while gripping a fresh drink.
explanation.walkthrough: N is held inside the rearranged letters of swigs ale.
explanation.definitionFit: A wineglass is a stemmed glass vessel for holding wine, so a container for drink.

clue.text: Fine to abandon wind instrument and stringed instrument

indicators.note: abandon means leave behind, so that letter departs from the instrument's name

blocks.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
the flute is a woodwind instrument

explanation.surface: A musician is happy to give up a wind instrument for a stringed one.
explanation.walkthrough: FLUTE without F gives LUTE. 'Fine' looks like approval, but it is the letter F.
explanation.definitionFit: A lute is a plucked string instrument with a pear-shaped body, popular in the Renaissance.

clue.text: Opening of concerto by aspiring, but not good, composer

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
but not means without, so the letter for good is left out

blocks.note: the first letter of concerto
aspiring means hoping
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A would-be composer's concerto starts promisingly but is not much good.
explanation.walkthrough: C then HOPING without its G gives CHOPIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Frédéric Chopin was the Polish Romantic composer famed for his piano works.

clue.text: Severely criticise medicine or remedy, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter of the preceding word is kept

blocks.note: a pill is a dose of medicine
taken as written
the last letter of remedy

explanation.surface: A critic slams a medicine or cure, at the end of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: To pillory is to expose someone to public ridicule and attack, from the old wooden pillory frame.

clue.text: Seduce bloke, casting off initial reserve

indicators.note: casting off the initial means throwing away the opening letter of the word before

blocks.note: a gent is a gentleman, a man or bloke
ice is cool reserve or aloofness of manner

explanation.surface: A man woos someone by first dropping his reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: GENT loses its G, then ICE. 'Initial reserve' reads as shyness at first, but initial goes with casting off; bloke is British slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice is to lure or tempt someone, so it is a close synonym of seduce.

clue.text: Swallow everything in ice-cream

indicators.note: in places the preceding word inside the following one

blocks.note: the sum is the whole amount, everything
a cone is an ice-cream cornet

explanation.surface: Eat up every bit of the ice cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ice-cream' here is the cornet it is served in, not the ice cream itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To consume food is to eat or swallow it, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Decline initially for everyone

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the word next to it is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of for
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Things go downhill for everybody at first.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall is a drop or decrease, as in a fall in prices, so it matches decline as a noun or verb.

clue.text: A person from eg Kelso racecourse

blocks.note: taken as written
Kelso is a town in the Scottish Borders, so its people are Scots

explanation.surface: A Borders native heads to the races.
explanation.walkthrough: Kelso is a market town in southern Scotland, which itself has a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is the famous English racecourse in Berkshire, home of Royal Ascot.

clue.text: Feature of engagement ring some gent waved about

indicators.note: something waved about is flung this way and that, so its letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man proudly flourishes the engagement ring he has bought.
explanation.definitionFit: An engagement ring is typically set with a precious stone such as a diamond, its central feature.

clue.text: Prepare for succession

blocks.note: first meaning: to get ready, coach or practise
second meaning: a series, as in a sequence of events or thought

explanation.surface: Groom someone to take over the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests royal succession; 'for' merely links the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Train is a verb for preparing by practice and a noun for a connected series, as in a train of thought.

clue.text: Company guy brought in excellent award

indicators.note: brought in means placed inside, so the first two pieces go within the word for excellent

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
a lad is a young man, a guy
ace means excellent

explanation.surface: A firm's employee was taken on and won a top prize.
explanation.walkthrough: Company and guy both sit inside the word for excellent; 'brought in' reads like hiring staff.
explanation.definitionFit: An accolade is an honour or token of praise, so it is a synonym of award.

clue.text: One unable to fly, being stuck in the mud

indicators.note: being stuck in says the answer is lodged inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A creature is grounded because it is bogged down in mud.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large Australian bird that cannot fly, so it is one unable to fly.

clue.text: Lean against brass instrument that's overturned

indicators.note: something overturned is upended, so the instrument's name is read back to front

blocks.note: the tuba is the largest brass instrument

explanation.surface: Someone props themselves on a tuba that has toppled over.
explanation.walkthrough: TUBA read backwards gives ABUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that abut touch along a border or rest against each other, close to leaning against.

clue.text: Hold off, for example, seizing time

indicators.note: to seize something is to grab hold of it, so the outer word wraps around the letter for time

blocks.note: say is used to introduce an example
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Delay, for instance by grabbing more time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For example' is not a link phrase here: it supplies the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay an execution or judgment is to postpone or hold it off.

clue.text: Waste soldiers, bringing in northern soldiers, after reflection

indicators.note: bringing in means taking inside, so the letter for northern goes within the soldiers
a reflection shows things back to front, so the second soldiers are read in reverse

blocks.note: a squad is a small group of soldiers
N is the abbreviation for northern
RE, the Royal Engineers, is a corps of British Army soldiers

explanation.surface: A general squanders his troops by drafting in northern ones after some thought.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers appears twice for two different units: a small group, then the Royal Engineers. 'After reflection' sounds like careful thought, but it signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To squander resources is to use them wastefully, so it is a synonym of the verb waste.
